tasks.spec:
You are building a small billed-probe tool (offline until a human confirms) in freytag-forge (Python 3.12). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. No network, no model call, no uv: `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example`, run `.venv/bin/python`. Do not git commit. You never make a live call. NEVER print, log or write any credential value. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: new scripts/ringer/environment_narration/jev_boarding_probe.py and new tests/test_jev_boarding_probe.py. Never edit any other file. Read first: storygame/runtime/jev.py (JevClient: POST {worker}/jev with {input:{state,questions}}, Bearer token, answers dict), storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py (boards_vehicle builds a question and reads answers[key]['noul']), scripts/ringer/environment_narration/smoke_direct.py (CLI shape, --dry/--run/--report, --confirm, --max-calls, partial rows written after every call, credential-leak guard), tests/test_environment_smoke_direct.py (hermetic test style).

PURPOSE: measure how the Jev boarding classifier answers a labeled set of player commands, comparing the OLD question wording (control) with the CURRENT boards_vehicle wording (another task is rewording it; import and call the live function, do not copy it).

BUILD, TESTS FIRST:
1. COMMANDS: a module constant of (command, expected_boards: bool) pairs in the player-input voice (docs/player-input-guide.md: imperative, `my` for the player's own things). The vehicle name for every question is `Kristin's truck`. expected True: 'Go out to my truck.', 'Go to my truck.', 'Head to my truck.', 'Get in my truck.', 'Climb into my truck.', 'Sit in my truck.', 'Drive my truck to town.', 'Go out to the truck.', 'Go to the truck.', 'Get into the truck.', 'Drive the truck to the house.', 'Start my truck.'. expected False: 'Walk over to my truck.', 'Walk up to my truck.', 'Approach my truck.', 'Step up to my truck.', 'Walk over to the truck.', 'Look through the truck window.', 'Examine my truck.', 'Open the truck door.', 'Touch the hood of my truck.', 'Check the tires on my truck.', 'Look at the passenger seat of my truck.', 'Leave my truck.', 'Get out of my truck.'.
2. ARMS: `old` = a literal copy in this file of the boards_vehicle question as it exists in git HEAD today (instructions 'Decide whether the command has the player go to the vehicle, get into it, sit in it, or drive it.', criteria true 'The command means going to the vehicle, getting into it, sitting in it, or driving it.', false 'The command only looks at, touches, or talks about the vehicle, or leaves it.'; type noul; key boards_vehicle; state {'command': ..., 'vehicle': ...}), kept as a named constant; `current` = call storygame.runtime.jev_questions.boards_vehicle(ask, command, vehicle) with a wrapping `ask` that records the raw answers object. Both arms send state {command, vehicle}. Raw answer = answers['boards_vehicle']['noul'] when present; predicted = noul_yes (storygame.runtime.jev), None when unusable.
3. CLI: `--dry --out PATH` prints the plan (calls = commands x arms x --samples, default samples 2; 25 commands x 2 arms x 2 = 100) and writes it, no network. `--run --confirm --max-calls K --out ROWS` requires CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL and CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN read only from the environment (never print or write their values; scan outputs for them like smoke_direct does), refuses without --confirm or if calls exceed K (default 100), interleaves round-robin command by command (old then current, sample by sample), uses JevClient with its default timeout, NO retries, writes the full rows file after EVERY call (partial rows survive), and stops at once on the first None answer caused by an HTTP 429 or any status >= 400 only if the client exposes it; JevClient.ask returns None for every failure, so count None as an unusable row and stop after 3 consecutive unusable rows (record the stop reason). Row fields: call_index, arm, command, expected, sample, raw_noul, predicted, correct (None when unusable), latency_ms. `--report --rows PATH --out MD` renders ALL rows (every call, correct or not), per arm: correct / total, unusable count, accuracy on expected-True and on expected-False separately, latency min/median/max, then a table of every command with its answers per arm and sample, and a section listing every wrong or unusable row.
4. TESTS (hermetic; socket and urllib patched to fail; fake opener injected via JevClient(opener=...)): plan size 100 and 50 with --samples 1; --run refuses without --confirm, without env URL/token, or over --max-calls; a fake opener answering by command text exercises both arms, rows written after each call, interleave order, an unusable answer, stop after 3 consecutive unusable rows, no retry of a failed call, report lists every row and the wrong ones, and no credential value appears in rows, report or stdout. See them fail, then build. FINISH: ruff check and ruff format both files; run `--dry` with dummy env values and report the calls.
tasks.check: cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge && export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example && set -o pipefail && P=.venv/bin/python && S=scripts/ringer/environment_narration && $P -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_jev_boarding_probe.py tests/test_jev_questions.py 2>&1 | tee /tmp/env-jevprobe.out | tail -5 && ! grep -Eq '[0-9]+ (failed|error|xfailed)' /tmp/env-jevprobe.out && env CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN=dummy-token-xyz $P $S/jev_boarding_probe.py --dry --out /tmp/env-jevprobe-plan.json | tail -3 && $P -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/env-jevprobe-plan.json'));s=json.dumps(d);assert len(d['calls'])==100,len(d['calls']);assert 'dummy-token-xyz' not in s" && (env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN $P $S/jev_boarding_probe.py --run --confirm --out /tmp/env-jevprobe-refuse.json; test $? -ne 0) && git diff --quiet -- data docs && $P -m ruff check $S/jev_boarding_probe.py tests/test_jev_boarding_probe.py && $P -m ruff format --check $S/jev_boarding_probe.py tests/test_jev_boarding_probe.py
